chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'I am an old man with many dependents, weak in strength, and possessing little wealth. Is there any assistance for my time?' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) looked at his companions, and his companions looked at him. He said: 'He has made us hear the speech, and made you all hear it.' Then a man stood up to him and said: 'I was like you yesterday.' So he took him to his house and gave him an ingot of gold. They used to trade with the ingot, which was gold and silver. The old man said: 'Is this all of it?' He said: 'Yes.' The old man said: 'I accept your ingot, for I am neither a jinn nor a human, but I am a Messenger from Allah to test you. I found you to be grateful, so may Allah recompense you with good.'

key_terms.تِبْرٍ: Gold (specifically refined gold used as currency)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the man who tested the Prophet's companion with an ingot of gold?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the practice of *Ibtila* (divine testing) through the Prophet’s companions, where a companion’s spontaneous generosity is tested by a figure claiming to be a divine messenger. In Shia scholarly tradition, this narrative highlights the virtue of *Shukr* (gratitude) and the spiritual reality that material wealth is often a means to test one’s character and thankfulness rather than an end in itself. The companion’s immediate acceptance of the gold as a test, rather than questioning its source, underscores the ideal of sincere, uncalculated charity (*Sadaqah*).
